dct_description_sm: This simulation experiment aims to evaluate the effects of browsing and climate changes on an important summer resource for caribou, the dwarf shrub Betula glandulosa. Understanding how these factors will affect forage availability is essential in a context of local and global decline of caribou populations (Vors and Boyce 2009) and warming of the tundra. Betula glandulosa cover is increasing in Nunavik (Tremblay et al. 2012, Ropars and Boudreau 2012) but this increase could be kept in check by heavy browsing pressure in some areas. Alternatively, we do not know how browsing and climate change interact to affect the availability of forage in the summer ground of caribou.
dct_title_s: Experimental browsing and climate change effects on Betula glandulosa in Nunavik
